item.title: Dopaminergic System: A Potential Therapeutic Target for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Diseases
item.description: Dopamine is a critical neurotransmitter involved in the regulation of motor control, cognition, reward processing, motivation, and neuroendocrine functions. Increasing evidence indicates that disturbances in dopaminergic neurotransmission contribute significantly to the pathogenesis of major neurodegenerative disorders, particularly Parkinson's Disease (PD) and Alzheimer's Disease (AD). The dopaminergic system comprises specialized neuronal populations, dopamine receptors, and transporter...

item.title: Vector versus scalar beams in atmospheric turbulence: scintillation index and average received intensity
item.description: The performance of free-space optical systems is impaired by atmospheric turbulence. Recently, vector beams have been considered more robust against atmospheric turbulence than scalar beams because their orthogonally polarized components can exhibit partially uncorrelated fluctuations. However, it remains unclear whether this advantage is fundamental or depends on the specific scalar reference used for comparison. In this work, we compare arbitrary vector beams with their constructed scalar...

item.title: Amikacin activity against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae without phenotypic aminoglycoside resistance: impact of aminoglycoside-modifying enzyme (AME) gene aac(6')-Ib-cr in vitro and in vivo
item.description: CONCLUSION: Carriage of aac(6')-Ib-cr was associated with reduced amikacin efficacy despite phenotypic susceptibility, independently of amikacin MIC, consistent with a treatment effect modifier rather than a binary resistance determinant. Genotyping of aac(6')-Ib-cr may help guide aminoglycoside use in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infections.

item.title: Musical Aptitude as a Predictor of Rhythm Production in Second Language Speech
item.description: This study examined the role of musical aptitude in predicting second language (L2) rhythm production at both word and sentence levels. To investigate the predictors of L2 English rhythmic performance, 60 Korean learners of English (age range: 18-31 years; M = 24.87, SD = 3.34) were recruited from South Korea. All participants completed a background questionnaire, a linguistic task, and a musical task. In the linguistic task, participants listened to recordings of 10 nonce words and 20 English...

item.title: Meningioma harboring IDH1 R132H mutation: a case report
item.description: Meningiomas are the most common primary central nervous system tumors. Monosomy of chromosome 22 is the most frequently reported genetic abnormality in meningioma and the occurrence of IDH1 mutations in meningioma is exceedingly rare. We report an uncommon case of IDH1 R132H-mutant meningioma. A 69-year-old man presented with two intracranial masses, one of which was identified as an IDH1 R132H-mutant meningioma by next-generation sequencing and further confirmed by pyrosequencing and...

item.title: Reliability-weighted patch learning for synthetic CT reconstruction in head and neck adaptive radiotherapy: A proof-of-concept study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: HQ-PatchNet provides a computationally efficient and clinically promising approach for daily CBCT-guided online ART by improving CBCT-to-sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed. Further contour-based, multi-institutional, and multi-site validation remains necessary to confirm its broader clinical utility.

item.title: Radical Resection Versus Organ-Preserving Local Excision for Rectal Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor: The Role of Neoadjuvant Imatinib
item.description: CONCLUSION: LE may provide acceptable recurrence control and potential functional advantages in selected patients. For large rectal GISTs, LE may be considered after adequate tumor downsizing with neoadjuvant imatinib.

item.title: Crystallographic Alignment Reshapes the Electronic Landscape and Enhances Charge Transport in Indium Gallium Oxide Thin-Film Transistors
item.description: Amorphous indium gallium zinc oxide thin-film transistors are widely used in high-end organic light-emitting diode displays. However, their intrinsic mobility-stability trade-off fundamentally limits further performance scaling. Crystallized oxide semiconductors have emerged as a promising pathway to overcome this constraint, yet the relative roles of crystallinity and crystallographic alignment remain unclear. Here, we systematically compare amorphous, random-polycrystalline, and highly aligned...

item.title: Presence, Social Capital, Social Isolation in Virtual Environments: The Role of Extraversion in Shaping Relational Outcomes
item.description: Virtual environment communication has been increasingly discussed as a potential means of addressing social isolation, yet little is known about how different forms of presence become relational resources. This study examines how physical presence and social presence in virtual environments are associated with social isolation through virtual-environment bonding and bridging social capital, and whether these relationships differ by users' level of extraversion. Data were collected from 500...

item.title: Angle-tunable air-gap Fabry-Pérot cavities for inline spectroscopy and hyperspectral imaging
item.description: In conventional spectrometers and hyperspectral imaging systems, the angle-of-incidence dependence of the spectral response is typically regarded as undesirable, as it leads to unintended spectral shifts that require calibration across the field of view. Here, we demonstrate a spectral-scanning platform enabling both inline spectroscopy and hyperspectral imaging by harnessing the strong angular dependence of an air-gap Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity as an intrinsic degree of freedom for spectral...

item.title: Model-fitting perspective on the robustness and speed of CLASS in reflection matrix microscopy
item.description: Closed-loop accumulation of single scattering (CLASS) recovers the input and output pupil aberrations from intrinsic tissue reflections, even under strong multiple scattering. Its central principle is to maximize the correlation among the ballistic waves in a measured reflection matrix, so that elements sharing the same momentum transfer add coherently. Here we recast CLASS as the solution of a model-fitting problem. We show that correlation maximization is equivalent to a least-squares fit of...

item.title: Sagging Peribursal Fat Sign as a Highly Specific Sonographic Finding to Diagnose Full-Thickness Supraspinatus Tendon Tear
item.description: CONCLUSION: In chronic shoulder pain patients with inconclusive direct ultrasonographic findings, the SPFS was a highly specific adjunctive sign for detecting full-thickness supraspinatus tendon tears. Although inter-reader agreement between experienced readers was moderate, overall agreement was fair, suggesting that experience may be important for reliable SPFS recognition.

item.title: Subtype-Specific Treatment of Autoimmune Myocarditis: Current Evidence and Clinical Approach
item.description: Autoimmune myocarditis presents a distinct therapeutic challenge: similar clinical syndromes may arise from fundamentally different immune mechanisms and therefore require different treatments. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence for the management of giant cell myocarditis, eosinophilic myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis, systemic autoimmune disease-associated myocarditis, immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis, and virus-negative immune-mediated lymphocytic...

item.title: Phosphine Catalyzed Anti-Selective Diborylation of Ynones with an Unsymmetrical Diboron Reagent
item.description: Organoboron compounds are among the most versatile synthetic intermediates, yet the direct diborylation of ynones remains elusive because the corresponding α-boryl ketone intermediates are intrinsically unstable. Herein, this challenge is addressed through reagent design rather than increased reactivity. An electronically differentiated unsymmetrical diboron reagent selectively installs the less Lewis acidic Bmdan unit at the α-position, while N-methylation suppresses premature proton transfer...

item.title: 10-fs-level laser-to-RF timing jitter of a directly diode-pumped Ti:sapphire oscillator
item.description: We demonstrate 10-fs-level laser-to-RF synchronization of a directly diode-pumped Kerr-lens mode-locked Ti:sapphire oscillator operating at 79.333 MHz, the 36th subharmonic of the PAL-XFEL 2.856-GHz RF reference. Pump-dependent free-running phase-noise measurements were used to identify a low-jitter operating condition. The oscillator delivered 117 mW of average output power, 44-fs pulses, an 18-nm optical bandwidth, and 0.5% RMS power fluctuations over 10 h without active pump-power...

item.title: Porto-Sinusoidal Vascular Disorder and Sinusoidal Obstructive Syndrome Might Have Similar Pathogenesis and Clinical Presentation
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Association of Self-Reported Clinical Behavior With Guideline Adherence in Schizophrenia and Major Depressive Disorder After Guideline Education
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Post-training self-reported CB scores were weakly associated with patient-level GAR. Given the cross-sectional, unadjusted analysis and the non-independence of patients treated by the same psychiatrist, these findings do not establish CB as a reliable proxy for actual clinical practice.

item.title: ROS Is Necessary for Dormancy Breaking in Fission Yeast Spores, While Its Downregulation by Sod1 Is Crucial for Later Events
item.description: Fission yeast spores adapt to nutrient deprivation by entering a dormant state. Upon exposure to nutrients, spores initiate germination, followed by proliferation. However, the molecular mechanisms that govern germination remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate that an optimal level of reactive oxygen species (ROS) facilitates germination progression, with the level decreasing as germination proceeds. Observations using ROS fluorescent probes indicated that intracellular ROS was relatively...

item.title: Resuscitation and 30-day postoperative mortality in acute type A aortic dissection: A cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection, combined preoperative and intraoperative resuscitation for ≥15 min was associated with higher 30-day mortality, and the risk increased with resuscitation duration. These findings provide prognostic information rather than a criterion for withholding surgery.

item.title: Intestinal Permeability in Irritable Bowel Syndrome With and Without Comorbid Conditions: Results From the European DISCOvERIE Cohort
item.description: BACKGROUND: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a disorder of gut-brain interaction often accompanied by psychiatric and/or somatic comorbidities. Intestinal-barrier dysfunction has been implicated in IBS pathophysiology. However, the contribution of psychiatric and somatic comorbidities to intestinal permeability remains unclear. We aimed to assess intestinal permeability in a large multicentric cohort of IBS patients with and without psychiatric and/or somatic comorbidities, compared with...

item.title: Beyond Self-Report: Adding Wearable Physiological Data to Predict Dietary Restriction in Anorexia Nervosa
item.description: CONCLUSION: Self-reported negative affect provided more information for predicting restriction than the physiological signals examined in this study. These findings suggest that self-report currently offers greater utility than wearable-derived stress physiology for identifying affect-related risk for restriction.

item.title: Stable Iodine Knowledge and Preferred Information Sources Among Parents in Fukushima Prefecture After the 2011 Nuclear Disaster
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Substantial knowledge gaps existed regarding stable iodine prophylaxis, particularly distribution methods. Health professionals, as the most trusted information source, may play a key role in addressing these gaps by communicating preparedness information to communities.

item.title: Placental Histological Lesions in Monochorionic Twins With Selective Fetal Growth Restriction Versus Growth-Restricted Singletons: A Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The smaller twin's placental territory in sFGR showed lesions consistent with placental insufficiency, with prevalences of MVM and chronic inflammation comparable to FGR singletons and increased prevalence of FVM. These findings suggest that placental insufficiency may be involved in the pathophysiology of sFGR alongside unequal sharing.

item.title: Number of Liver Metastases Stratifies Prognosis in Synchronous Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer
item.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy, frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage. While systemic chemotherapy is the standard of care for metastatic disease, clinical outcomes vary considerably among patients. Oligo-recurrence, limited metachronous metastasis potentially suitable for aggressive local treatment, has emerged as a clinically relevant concept associated with prolonged survival in selected patients, while the prognostic significance of synchronous...

item.title: La preuve par la Chine? Jesuit networks, academic politics, and the shape of the Earth in 1730s Paris
item.description: This article argues that the Maupertuis-Cassini controversy over the shape of the Earth in the 1730s was intricately connected to Eurasian intellectual networks and academic politics. It focuses on the alliance of two Parisian pro-Cassini savants, Dortous de Mairan and Nicolas Fréret, and on their private correspondence with French Jesuits Antoine Gaubil and Dominique Parrenin in Beijing. Through these Eurasian connections, this article examines how Qing cartographic information was mobilized...

item.title: Depth estimation in fluorescence microscopy using degree of polarization
item.description: Accurate axial depth estimation in fluorescence microscopy remains challenging in non-interferometric systems due to weak signals and strong background noise. Here, we investigate the depth-dependent behavior of the degree of polarization (DOP) and demonstrate its applicability for axial localization under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions. By formulating a noise-aware model based on the cross-spectral density matrix that explicitly incorporates unpolarized background fluorescence and...

item.title: Autonomous in-silico inorganic materials discovery via multi-agent physics-aware scientific reasoning
item.description: Conventional machine learning approaches accelerate in-silico inorganic materials design via accurate property prediction and targeted material generation, yet they operate as single-shot models limited by the latent knowledge baked into their training data. A central challenge lies in creating an intelligent system capable of autonomously executing the full in-silico inorganic materials discovery cycle, from ideation and planning to experimentation and iterative refinement. We introduce...

item.title: An in vivo fluorescence imaging approach for real-time monitoring of ROS-associated oxidative responses in harvested lettuce leaves
item.description: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a key role in postharvest quality and senescence of fresh produce, yet their real-time monitoring in intact tissues remains challenging. In this study, we developed and evaluated an in vivo fluorescence imaging approach for monitoring ROS dynamics in whole harvested lettuce leaves using the ROS-sensitive probe 2', 7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate (H(2)DCF-DA). The stability of the probe and the sensitivity of the imaging system were first assessed under...

item.title: Association of physical frailty with cardiac conduction disorder events in the UK Biobank
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Physical frailty was associated with graded increases in incident CCD and related conduction outcomes, with excess risk evident at the prefrailty stage. Frailty assessment may help identify individuals with increased susceptibility, although the observational design does not establish causality or demonstrate that modifying frailty would reduce risk.

item.title: Long COVID shows IL-1 pathway dysregulation without a discrete circulating biomarker signature
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent and, often, disabling symptoms, yet its biological basis remains unclear. Multiple mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and persistence of SARS-CoV-2 components, have been proposed, although it is unknown whether these define distinct biological subtypes or overlapping processes.

item.title: Beyond eosinophil depletion: long-term clinical trajectory and durability of response to benralizumab in patients with severe eosinophilic asthma and CRSwNP: an 18-month real-world study (the BANDOR study)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The BANDOR study demonstrates that benralizumab can induce durable clinical remission in a specific subset of patients who maintain treatment adherence. The speed of response is domain specific, with physical symptoms improving before emotional and functional ones. A high initial eosinophilic burden is the primary determinant of a rapid response. These findings suggest that while randomized trials showed limited efficacy, Real-World data identifies a high disease burden phenotype...

item.title: Azole resistance among clinical Aspergillus fumigatus species complex isolates in Greece: first detection of TR46-mediated resistance and azole-resistant cryptic species
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although the clinical ARAf rate remains low in Greece, the first detection of pan-azole resistance associated with environmentally driven resistance mechanisms or cryptic species highlights the importance of surveillance, accurate species identification and routine AFST.

item.title: Revising the mechanism of visible-light Baeyer-Villiger oxidation: benzaldehyde is the active photoinitiator
item.description: The photoinitiating role of benzaldehyde in the Mukaiyama-based photocatalytic Baeyer-Villiger (B-V) oxidation is not yet evaluated. Here, we show that benzaldehyde itself acts as a photoinitiator, promoting B-V oxidation, highlighting that its intrinsic photoreactivity must be accounted for.

item.title: Identification of auxin response factor ARF27 as a regulator of maize root morphogenesis
item.description: Auxin is a central phytohormone that mediates root development. This study investigated the genetic basis of auxin-mediated primary root growth in Zea mays (maize) seedlings, which is not well-understood in this key cereal crop. To address this knowledge gap, 618 accessions from the Wisconsin Diversity panel were leveraged for a genome wide association study (GWAS) followed by reverse genetics and in silico gene regulatory network reconstruction (GRN). The GWAS identified several candidate genes...

item.title: Mixed Reality-Based Telemedicine for Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Remote Island Setting: A Pilot Feasibility Study (Nagasaki University Rheumatoid Arthritis Remote Medicine System, NURAS)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: NURAS was technically and operationally feasible for collaborative, specialist-supported RA care in a remote island setting. Larger controlled studies are needed to evaluate diagnostic agreement, acceptability, technical performance, cost, and clinical effectiveness.

item.title: Analysis of adverse events following immunization after immunization schedule adjustment for acellular DTaP combined vaccine among 6-year-old children in Hangzhou
item.description: In 2025, China adjusted national immunization schedule to administer a booster dose of acellular diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis combined vaccine (DTaP) to 6-year-old children, replacing the previously used diphtheria-tetanus combined vaccine (DT). Post-marketing safety surveillance of this newly implemented schedule is critical to evaluate the tolerability and safety of DTaP in this age group. To evaluate the epidemiological characteristics and safety of adverse events following immunization...

item.title: Lipid-inclusive metabolomics of infants born after suspected preterm labor according to whether delivery occurred preterm or at term: A prospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Cord blood metabolomic profiles differed between infants from pregnancies complicated by sPTL and infants from uncomplicated term pregnancies. The persistence of an intermediate metabolic profile among infants born at term after sPTL raises the possibility of a metabolic signature associated with the preceding episode of sPTL. However, the observational design and frequent antenatal corticosteroid exposure preclude the attribution of these differences specifically to sPTL. Larger...

item.title: Metabolic and Endocrine Modulation by a Novel 1,2,3,6-Tetrahydropyridine- Substituted 7-Azaindole Derivative in a Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome Rat Model
item.description: CONCLUSION: A1 significantly restored endocrine and hormonal markers, glucose, insulin, and dyslipidemia while enhancing FSHR gene expression; molecular docking predicted binding within the FSHR allosteric pocket, a finding not yet functionally validated. These results indicate that A1, a novel 7-azaindole derivative, may regulate reproductive and metabolic dysfunctions in PCOS through endocrine modulation and receptor-- mediated mechanisms, demonstrating significant therapeutic potential for...

item.title: Multifunctional Hyaluronic Acid-functionalized Liposomes for Targeted Astaxanthin Delivery in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cells
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that HA-functionalized liposomes can improve the delivery performance and anticancer potential of AST, providing a promising lipid-based nanoplatform for HCC-targeted therapy.

item.title: Long-Term Predictive Value of MRI Radiomics in Identifying Patients with Metastasis-Free Breast Cancer Over a 100-Month Follow-Up Period: A retrospective, observational study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Radiomics-based modeling using DCE-MRI and clinical data demonstrated potential in effectively predicting long-term metastatic risk in patients with breast cancer and identifying a subset of metastatic-free patients with favorable profiles who may benefit from less intensive surveillance.

item.title: Natural Medicines for Parkinson's Disease: A Bibliometric Analysis of Trends, Challenges, and Future Directions
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study provides the first systematic bibliometric overview of natural medicines in Parkinson's disease over the past two decades, revealing a paradigm shift from reductionist single-target approaches to holistic multi-target and multi-system strategies. These findings offer a valuable reference for neuropharmacological research on Parkinson's disease and clinical translation of natural products.

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Validation of a scale for deciding on the referral of patients with Parkinson's disease to a competence center for selection for interventional therapies
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The concise and user-friendly IT-PD score effectively assesses the critical criteria for selecting candidates for interventional therapy, thereby supporting timely referral decisions to specialized centers.

item.title: Genetic markers of stress susceptibility: From individual risk - to the differential sensitivity hypothesis. (Systematic review)
item.description: CONCLUSION: Recognizing genetic predisposition to stress introduces opportunities for personalized prevention and treatment of psychosomatic disorders. Advancing multigenic panels will enhance the effectiveness of risk stratification and facilitate the selection of tailored interventions.

item.title: Modifiable risk factors for Alzheimer's disease
item.description: Alzheimer's disease is a prominent medical and social challenge of our time and stands as the leading cause of dementia, resulting in significant disability for those affected. Since no etiotropic therapy is available, prioritizing primary and secondary prevention through the management of the key factors contributing to the development of Alzheimer's disease has become imperative for the medical community. In recent years, there has been an increasing focus on investigating modifiable risk...

item.title: Diagnostic Performance of BUU-Customized Whole-Exome Sequencing for Suspicious Thyroid Nodules: A Prospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: BUU-WES primarily functions as a rule-in test due to its high specificity. Its most clinically relevant application is in indeterminate thyroid nodules (Bethesda III/IV), where it serves as an adjunctive tool for risk stratification. Within this subgroup, diagnostic performance is further optimized in nodules ≥1 cm, where the improved NPV suggests potential rule-out applicability in appropriately selected patients.

item.title: The TOGETHER Model: A Next-Generation Integrated Framework for Communication in Healthcare
item.description: Communication is a core clinical competence that directly impacts treatment adherence and patient outcomes. Although excellent communication, coaching, and educational frameworks have been developed, they often operate in isolation, leaving clinicians to navigate between disparate approaches without a unifying reference. The TOGETHER Model is introduced in this study as a conceptual proposal that integrates and synthesizes established evidence-based communication practices and professional...

item.title: Primary Prevention Needs to Reduce Family Violence and Sexual Violence Among Older Adults: A Culture-Centered Study in Aotearoa New Zealand
item.description: Family and sexual violence are significant public health issues in Aotearoa New Zealand, but research examining prevention strategies is limited. Grounded in Dutta's culture-centered approach, this study examines the primary prevention needs of older adults to reduce family violence and sexual violence in Aotearoa New Zealand as part of a broader project that is co-developing a prevention framework among high-risk groups. Through 63 interviews with older adults in Aotearoa New Zealand,...

item.title: Dynamic Supercooled Crystal-Gels for Ultrafast, Reversible Mechanical Adaptative Materials
item.description: Endowing synthetic materials with adaptability and responsiveness to dynamically optimize their states represents a premier frontier in biomimetic science. However, achieving life-like, rapid yet reversible adaptation under benign triggers remains hindered by high reconfiguration energy or delayed structural recovery. In this work, we present dynamic supercooled crystal-gels that achieve ultrafast, reversible stiffening without requiring continuous energy input. Inspired by the tactile-triggered...

item.title: CGRP levels in autoimmune diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of its potential role as a biomarker
item.description: CONCLUSION: Circulating CGRP is elevated across specific autoimmune pathologies, functioning as a dynamic indicator of active neuro-immune inflammation rather than a static universal marker. Clinical implementation requires prospective, longitudinal studies and standardized, isoform-specific quantification assays.

item.title: Preparation of dual-ligand magnetic hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks and their application for enrichment of glycosylated and phosphorylated peptides
item.description: Protein glycosylation and phosphorylation are critical post-translational modifications （PTMs） that regulate protein conformation，activity，transport，localization，and cellular processes including growth，division，signal transduction，and metabolism. However，the low abundance and poor ionization efficiency of glycosylated and phosphorylated peptides in complex biological samples necessitate highly selective enrichment strategies prior to mass spectrometry analysis. In this study，we designed and...

item.title: Osteoarthritis-Microenvironment-Triggered Phase Alteration of Injectable Conductive Hydrogel for Attenuating Cartilage Degradation
item.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which contributes substantially to chondrocyte dysfunction, oxidative stress, and cartilage degradation. Although stimuli-responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for OA therapy, conventional hydrogel-based systems exhibit limited sensitivity and require external detection equipment, highlighting the need for a simple, sensitive, and directly observable monitoring system. To address these...

item.title: Videoconference-based cognitive behavioral therapy for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a pilot randomized controlled trial
item.description: Access to evidence-based psychological treatments for children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remains limited by therapist shortages and geographical barriers. Videoconference-based cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT) may provide an alternative to face-to-face CBT, but evidence in young populations is limited. This pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) examined the feasibility and preliminary treatment outcomes of vCBT for children and adolescents with ADHD in Japan....

item.title: Phenotype-driven approach for safinamide use in Parkinson's disease
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is now recognized as a multisystem neurodegenerative disorder marked by the progressive disintegration of large-scale functional networks in the brain, a phenomenon termed connectomopathy. The clinical heterogeneity of PD reflects the distinct patterns of neuronal ensemble involvement in individual patients, contributing to both motor and non-motor symptoms. This perspective highlights the necessity of a phenotype-driven approach when selecting anti-Parkinsonian...

item.title: Anhedonia in Parkinson's disease: findings from the first national clinical and statistical study of motor and non-motor associations
item.description: CONCLUSION: Anhedonia is a prevalent non-motor manifestation of PD, identified in most patients in this cohort. It is most strongly associated with depressive symptoms, which remain independently significant in multivariate analysis. Anhedonia is not directly related to motor severity, disease duration, dyskinesias, or functional independence. These results suggest that anhedonia is primarily an affective non-motor component of PD and should be specifically assessed in clinical practice.

item.title: Multimodal biomarkers of Parkinson's disease risk in essential tremor. (A prospective cohort study)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The risk of Parkinson's disease onset in patients with ET-plus is determined by a combination of multimodal biomarkers. The prospective identification of 15 patients who converted supports classifying this subgroup as a high-risk phenotype that warrants ongoing monitoring and comprehensive evaluation.

item.title: Serum markers of intestinal and blood-brain barrier permeability (zonulin and claudin-5) in patients with Parkinson's disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: Assessing specific changes in intestinal and blood-brain barrier permeability markers in patients with PD is a significant area of research for understanding the disease's pathogenesis. Further investigation is necessary to predict disease progression and to identify potential targets for pathogenetic therapy.

item.title: Molecular biomarkers for multiple system atrophy. (A systematic review)
item.description: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is a rare, rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disorder. Early diagnosis remains challenging because of clinical heterogeneity and symptom overlap with Parkinson's disease and other atypical parkinsonian syndromes. This systematic review synthesizes current evidence on molecular biomarkers of MSA in biological fluids, including cerebrospinal fluid and blood plasma, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and...

item.title: Epidemiology of Parkinson's disease in a multinational region of Russia: a population-based study in the republic of Sakha (Yakutia)
item.description: CONCLUSION: The increase in reported incidence and expansion of high-prevalence areas likely reflect case accumulation in older age groups and improved detection due to better access to specialized care. These findings highlight the need to improve the regional PD registry, standardize recording criteria, and proactively identify patients in remote areas.

item.title: Consensus on definitions, terminology, classification of dystonia, and clinical guidelines. Part 2. Etiology and pathogenesis (Axis II). Novel genetic classification
item.description: This article presents an adapted Russian-language version of the 2025 International Consensus on the Classification of Dystonia, with particular emphasis on etiology and pathogenesis (Axis II). The revised classification integrates recent advances in the understanding of the biological mechanisms underlying dystonia. Axis II distinguishes between genetic and acquired etiologies, clarifies the anatomical classification of nervous system lesions, and introduces a new category for pathogenetic...

item.title: Consensus on definitions, terminology, classification of dystonia, and clinical guidelines. Part 1. Historical context, definitions, terminology, and clinical characteristics (Axis i)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This consensus unifies terminology and clinical assessment of dystonia, adapts international guidelines for Russian-speaking practice, and supports standardized diagnosis, phenomenological description, and rational therapy selection.

item.title: Homojunction Back Contacts Enable Efficient Cu<sub>2</sub>O Photocathodes
item.description: Enhancing carrier separation and extraction is crucial to achieve efficient metal oxide photoelectrodes for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. Here, we report a highly efficient Cu(2)O photocathode based on p^(+)/p back-contact homojunction. The homojunction significantly enhances hole-selective extraction while suppressing electron backflow at the back-contact interface, leading to marked improvements in PEC performance. The optimized photocathode delivers a hydrogen evolution reaction...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Segment-Specific Occlusion of Retrieved Plastic Biliary Stents: Direct Quantification and Microbial and Material Determinants
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Plastic stent occlusion is segment-dependent, predominantly affecting the proximal portion, and is associated with microbiological and material-related factors. Direct quantification may help optimize stent design and management.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Compared with DXA, continuous sagittal CT images improved detection of greatest vertebral height loss, especially for Grade 1 reductions. When applying 2D criteria to CT scans, clinicians should be cautious of a tendency to overestimate vertebral height loss.

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Equitable Visibility Optimization: Discovering Credible Health Information in an Era of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Search
item.description: While artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots provide quick answers to health questions, they raise equity concerns about what information is visible, who controls it, and how it is presented. This perspective examines AI as an information intermediary and highlights areas for improvement. We introduce Equitable Visibility Optimization (EVO), a public health framework that organizes the distinct responsibilities of health organizations, AI developers, information consumers, clinicians, and...

item.title: Single-cell Sequencing Reveals Multi-omics Dynamics During Lymph Node Metastasis in Breast Cancer
item.description: Single-cell sequencing and analysis have advanced our understanding of intra-tumoral heterogeneity for breast cancer lymph node metastasis. However, how alterations at multi-omics levels coordinate together in a single tumor cell to drive metastasis remains unclear. Here we performed single-cell multi-omics sequencing of paired primary tumors and metastatic lymph nodes from breast cancer patients. This enabled a comprehensive reconstruction of dynamic molecular landscapes by simultaneously...

item.title: Fracture Network Structure and Groundwater Seepage Characteristics in the Karst of Northern China
item.description: The high heterogeneity and anisotropy of karst aquifer media are key scientific issues that constrain accurate simulation of groundwater flow in karst regions. Taking the typical Cambrian-Ordovician karst water system in northern China as an example, this study systematically reveals the multi-scale structural characteristics of karst fractures and their controlling mechanisms on seepage behavior using high-precision micro-focus CT scanning, three-dimensional digital core reconstruction,...

item.title: Can Hormesis Facilitate Biological Invasions?
item.description: During biological invasions, introduced organisms are exposed to multiple, sequential environmental stressors across invasion stages. Although stress is traditionally viewed as a source of damage and environmental filtering, exposure within a hormetic zone may induce a persistent state that improves performance under subsequent challenges. Here, we critically review the available evidence for stress-induced hormesis in invasion-relevant contexts. We then develop a four-stage framework linking...

item.title: CAR T and NK cell therapy for acute myeloid leukemia
item.description: Adoptive cell therapy has emerged as a powerful approach for treating hematologic malignancies. Among these strategies, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has demonstrated remarkable clinical efficacy, especially for treating B cell malignancies. Several CAR T cell products have been approved for clinical use. Additionally, CAR-engineered natural killer (CAR NK) cells have recently been developed and have shown promising results in clinical trials for treating B-cell malignancies....

item.title: Prevalence and Burden of Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction in Nigeria: Results From the Rome Foundation Global Epidemiology Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: DGBI are prevalent and impactful in Nigeria, in line with studies from other parts of the world that utilized the face-to-face survey methodology. More studies are needed to further understand the distribution and impact of DGBI in Nigeria and other similar countries around the world where they are understudied.

item.title: Cortical Adaptation to Muscle Fatigue Does Not Alter Early Proprioceptive Processing in Primary Sensorimotor Cortex
item.description: Muscle fatigue potentially interferes with proprioceptive afference from peripheral "movement sensors"-the proprioceptors, which may hinder crucial sensorimotor integration and thus movement performance. item.description: The temporal resolution of medical imaging sequences used to drive patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations remains limited, typically providing 10-20 frames per cardiac cycle. item.description: Extensive research has demonstrated that electrical stimulation (ES) accelerates wound healing by promoting cellular proliferation and migration. However, the delivery of continuous and noninvasive ES to the wound site remains a major challenge. Conventional ES devices generally depend on external power supplies and often suffer from limited biocompatibility. To address these limitations, we developed an innovative wound healing strategy that integrates ES with biocompatible materials....

item.description: The mechanisms underlying the drag produced by soft biofilms are complex due to the interaction between the flow and the biological communities. To fully understand this phenomenon, hydrodynamic studies need to be paired with biological analysis involving the characteristics of what is present on the drag-producing surfaces. item.description: Mixed-anion chalcogenide compounds, particularly Pb(2)SbS(2)I(3), hold promise for optoelectronic applications owing to their chemical stability and tunable electronic properties. However, their performance is intrinsically limited by disordered polyhedral connectivity and native defects inherent to sulfohalide structures, which is challenging to optimize through conventional chemical methods. item.title: Application of orthognathic surgery in the treatment of severe adult obstructive sleep apnea
item.description: Orthognathic surgery is one of the most effective surgical techniques for the treatment of severe obstructive sleep apnea （OSA） in adults, and its application is becoming increasingly widespread. The application of strategies and techniques such as the surgery-first approach, segmental osteotomy, and counterclockwise rotation of the jaws can maximize the therapeutic potential of orthognathic surgery for severe OSA in adults. item.description: Persistent bacterial infection has become life-threatening challenge worldwide. Bacterial biofilm formation, causing induced antimicrobial resistance and suppressive immune microenvironment, is one of the critical pathways leading chronic and persistent infection. Herein, an integrated microneedle patch harboring neutrophil membrane and antibiotics is designed to elicit therapeutic in-situ immunization for the management of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection. When applied on...

item.title: Risks of Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Individuals with Alopecia Areata: A Case-Control Study
item.description: Alopecia areata (AA) is a common autoimmune condition, affecting both physical and psychological well-being. IBD, encompassing ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, is marked by chronic intestinal inflammation. Since AA is associated with numerous autoimmune diseases, a potential link between AA and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has been suggested, though evidence remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between AA and IBD using data from a nationwide retrospective...

item.title: Mapping Gadolinium-based Contrast Agent Residues in the Rat Kidney
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first comprehensive spatially resolved characterization of renal GBCA residues at an early and a late time point. GBCA residues exhibited specific intrarenal distribution patterns and distinct changes in these patterns over the course of their elimination. Our findings of specific retention patterns suggest that renal microanatomy and local physicochemical conditions play critical roles in GBCA retention. item.title: Grain-Boundary Engineering for Electrocatalysis: From Precise Structural Analysis to Reaction-Pathway Regulation
item.description: Amid efforts toward carbon neutrality and rapid renewable energy development, CO(2)/CO electroreduction and water electrolysis have emerged as critical pathways for carbon resource recycling and green hydrogen production. However, CO(2) and CO electroreduction reaction (CO(2)RR/CORR) remain limited by complex multielectron-transfer pathways, insufficient product selectivity, and poor stability at high current densities. item.title: Three-dimensional-printed heart models as medical educational tools in cardiac catheterisation: randomised controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: Three-dimensional-printed heart models provide a feasible and cost-effective approach for teaching cardiac catheterisation in medical education. Their educational benefits appeared more evident among undergraduate medical students. Integrating such models according to learners' training stages and procedural complexity may further enhance training effectiveness.

item.title: Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibitor Use and Cancer Incidence Among UK Biobank Participants: A Prospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: RAS inhibitor use was not associated with overall cancer incidence in this large cohort of antihypertensive medication users. Although modest associations were observed between ARB use and prostate cancer incidence and between ACEI use and bladder cancer incidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in future studies.

item.title: From Pathogens to Therapeutics: Harnessing Parasite Nanomaterials in Precision Oncology
item.description: Parasites are one of the pathogens' threats to human and animal health, yet emerging evidence reveals their paradoxical potential as valuable therapeutic agents in oncology. Parasitic derivatives demonstrate remarkable tumor specificity, selectively eliminating malignant cells while sparing normal tissues. This review systematically summarizes the antitumor mechanisms and applications of major protozoan and helminth parasites investigated to date. The reviewed evidence is derived from in vitro...

item.title: Spin-Resolved Topology of Mem-Emitter Response
item.description: We develop a general framework for spin-resolved mem-emitters and illustrate it unequivocally using a monolayer MoSe2/clinochlore optoelectronic device. In mem-emitters, both the intensity and energy of light emission encode the history of external driving through slowly evolving internal state variables. item.title: Duodenal-Jejunal Bypass Stent Versus Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy in Patients With Obesity and MASLD: Short-Term Efficacy and Perioperative Safety in a Retrospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: DJBS produces moderate short-term weight loss with better perioperative safety, while LSG achieves greater weight reduction. Both interventions were associated with comparable short-term changes in liver-related biochemical markers.

item.title: Evaluating and Optimizing Mass Decarceration as a Pandemic Mitigation Strategy
item.description: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed the vulnerabilities of carceral systems as high-risk environments for disease transmission. In response, jurisdictions across the United States implemented mass decarceration policies aimed at reducing jail populations. This paper investigates such interventions and their optimal planning, leveraging system-theoretic insights. First, we empirically demonstrate the influence of jail population changes on COVID-19 infections by applying convergent cross mapping,...

item.title: The Association of Diet, Intestinal Microbial Starch Utilizers and Butyrate-Producers in Early Life
item.description: During the first year of life, infant diet changes from liquid to solid food. Resistant starch is one of the first complex carbohydrates available to gut microbiota. With the overall goal to gain mechanistic understanding on the development of microbial starch utilization capacity and its impact on fermentation activity, we investigated the interplay of diet, starch utilizers Ruminococcus bromii and Bifidobacterium adolescentis and the butyrate producer Anaerobutyricum hallii using samples from...

item.title: Dietary fibre intake and suicide in Japanese adults: the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study
item.description: Dietary fibre intake has been reported to be inversely associated with depression in a meta-analysis. However, most studies were cross-sectional, and none examined the association with suicide, a severe outcome of depression. We investigated the association of dietary fibre intake with suicide risk among Japanese adults. Participants were 40 630 men and 48 178 women aged 44-76 years who responded to the second survey (baseline of the present study) of the Japan Public Health Center-based...

item.title: Post-ovipositional staging series of the foveate, gold-dust day gecko, Phelsuma laticauda (Gekkota: Squamata)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: P. laticauda undergoes early asymmetric ocular remodeling and the prospective foveal region transiently elongates and retracts during the final third of embryonic development, a progression consistent with other foveate lizards and humans. These findings support day geckos as a promising model for understanding foveal development and potentially relevant disease pathways.

item.title: Nonlinear pluggable optics: digital signal processing-free intensity modulated direct detection links using analog photonic next generation reservoir computing
item.description: In this work, we propose and simulate a nonlinear pluggable optic (NLPO) transceiver that combines the low latency and low power consumption of linear pluggable optics (LPO) with the range and robustness of digital signal processing (DSP)-based transceivers. item.title: Wave-optics numerical simulation of atmospheric turbulence in 10,000-km-scale satellite-ground optical links with spatially adaptive phase screens
item.description: Atmospheric turbulence degrades satellite-ground optical links through scintillation, beam wander, power fluctuations, and wavefront distortion. Simulating approximately 10,000-km links is challenging because a finite turbulent atmosphere must be coupled to a long near-vacuum path. We propose a spatially adaptive phase-screen configuration based on equal log-amplitude variance and introduce a band-limited scaled multistep angular-spectrum method. item.title: 266 nm generation performance of NSBBF crystal improved by elevating the operating temperature
item.description: NaSr(3)Be(3)B(3)O(9)F(4) (NSBBF) crystal is a promising nonlinear optical (NLO) crystal for 266 nm ultraviolet (UV) generation by fourth-harmonic generation (FHG), whereas crystal cracking under nanosecond (ns) high-power pumping limits further power scaling. For this purpose, an effective route is analyzed and proposed in this paper that is moderate elevating the operating temperature of NSBBF crystal. When the crystal temperature was set at 100.9 ℃, and under the condition that all other...

item.title: Inverse design of multi-band terahertz metamaterial sensors with nested topologies via a transformer-conditioned variational autoencoder
item.description: Multi-band terahertz (THz) metamaterial sensors with nested topologies offer multiple resonance channels for complex sensing applications, but their inverse design is hindered by a high-dimensional coupled design space and the inherent one-to-many nature of the structure-to-spectrum mapping. Here, the inverse-design task is defined as generating nested sensor structures that reproduce prescribed bare absorption spectra. item.title: All-fiber quantum current transformer based on nitrogen-vacancy centers
item.description: High-voltage substations impose stringent requirements on current measurement, demanding simultaneously high electrical insulation and stable, high-precision performance. Here we propose and experimentally validate an all-fiber quantum current transformer based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond. item.description: Brillouin optical time-domain reflectometry based on the short-time Fourier transform (STFT-BOTDR) enables rapid acquisition of Brillouin gain spectra (BGSs). item.description: We propose a high-speed full-field tomographic imaging method based on Fourier fringe analysis (FFA) integrated with broadband multi-GHz electro-optic comb interferometry. The proposed approach eliminates measurement null points while simultaneously reconstructing amplitude and phase distributions from interference peak envelopes that are free of temporal carrier fringes along the depth-sweep direction, while transverse spatial carrier fringes are used for FFA. item.title: Thermal delay response and high-stability RF transfer in hollow-core fibers
item.description: The coherent operation of distributed radar systems requires stable radio frequency (RF) reference distribution among spatially separated nodes. In conventional single mode fiber (SMF) links, thermally induced delay variations often require active compensation, thereby increasing system complexity and limiting rapid deployment. item.description: This erratum corrects a formula error in the following paper: Opt. Express, 34(8), 15233 (2026). The affected figures and text have been revised. The other results and conclusions are unaffected by this correction.

item.title: Model-constrained nanoscale 3D cathodoluminescence reconstruction of InGaN LEDs via coupled electron-photon transport
item.description: Depth-resolved cathodoluminescence (DRCL) is widely used to probe semiconductor heterostructures, but voltage-dependent spectra are depth-convolved by the finite electron-matter interaction volume and photon transport across multilayer interfaces. Here we develop a model-constrained nanoscale three-dimensional (3D) CL reconstruction framework for InGaN LEDs based on multi-voltage scanning electron microscope (SEM) CL measurements and Monte Carlo electron-photon transport. item.title: Inverse design of a fiber-to-fiber integrated metasurface system for multiplexing and demultiplexing of orbital angular momentum modes
item.description: A two-way multiplexer (MUX) and demultiplexer (DEMUX) system to separate spatially overlapping OAM modes in a multi-mode fiber into spatially separated Gaussian modes in a multi-core fiber has been designed and modelled. The designed system consists of two silicon metasurfaces. Each metasurface consists of silicon nanopillars with spatially varying radii arranged on a square grid. item.description: This publisher's note contains a correction to [Opt. Express23(2), 1190 (2015)]. The article was corrected on 20 October 2026.

item.title: Advanced Solid-State Lasers 2025: feature issue introduction
item.description: This joint feature issue of Optics Express and Optical Materials Express presents 38 peer-reviewed articles associated with the Advanced Solid-State Lasers 2025 conference, held as part of the Optica Laser Congress in Prague, Czechia, from 19 to 23 October 2025. The collection reflects continuing progress in solid-state laser materials, laser architectures, ultrafast and high-power sources, nonlinear optics, and frequency conversion. item.title: Knowledge Gaps and Educational Needs Among Patients Receiving Long-Acting Injectable Cabotegravir/Rilpivirine: A Multisite Cross-Sectional Survey
item.description: Long-acting injectable antiretroviral therapy (LAI ART) offers an alternative to daily ART by mitigating adherence barriers such as pill fatigue and stigma. However, it introduces new challenges, including the need for continued engagement, clear communication, and understanding of the consequences of missed or delayed doses. Patient knowledge of these issues remains poorly characterized. Between June 1 and October 2, 2025, we administered a structured survey to individuals receiving LAI ART at...

item.title: Attitudes toward eating disorders among primary care physicians
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Attitudes toward eating disorders were broadly similar across diagnoses, but positive attitudes toward working with affected patients were uncommon. Education was consistently associated with more favorable attitudes and greater confidence in management, highlighting the potential value of continuing professional education and support for eating disorder care in primary care.

item.title: Moral distress and constraints (tied together)
item.description: Moral distress was (on one prominent reading) originally proposed as a phenomenon wherein nurses knew the right thing to do but were constrained from doing it. Since then, the concept has evolved to include a broader array of phenomena, notably including those where the nurse does not know the right thing to do. In this article I argue that this purported evolution has actually been a step in the wrong direction, and that we would do well to return to (one reading of) the original understanding...

item.title: An integrated CT/MRI diagnostic system for pancreatic cystic lesions that supports pathological classification and risk stratification
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SIRS-PCL is a pathology-based, quantitative decision-support system for preoperative pathological subtype classification and pathological risk stratification of surgically evaluated neoplastic PCLs.

item.description: Microorganisms, including bacteria, fungi, and viruses, can invade the human body, disrupt normal physiological functions, and trigger a variety of infectious diseases, currently posing a significant global health issue. item.title: Predictors of Antibiotic Overuse in Febrile Children: A Sub-analysis of the Prospective, Multicenter AutoPilot-Dx Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Diagnostic uncertainty contributes to antibiotic overuse, alongside clinical factors. Future studies should investigate the impact of improved diagnostic algorithms on antibiotic prescribing in patients with respiratory tract infections in whom physicians experience diagnostic uncertainty.

item.title: Bariatric Surgery as a Rescue Strategy After Semaglutide or Tirzepatide
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Bariatric surgery was associated with clinically meaningful 2-year weight loss after semaglutide or tirzepatide intolerance or inadequate response, with RYGB potentially offering greater benefit after inadequate response.

item.title: Silicone lymphadenopathy of the axilla: a potential for misdiagnosis as metastatic carcinoma on fine-needle aspiration cytology
item.description: Silicone lymphadenopathy is an uncommon but well-recognized complication of silicone implant placement resulting from migration of silicone to regional lymph nodes. In patients with prior breast implantation, silicone lymphadenopathy most commonly involves the axillary lymph nodes. Because axillary lymphadenopathy may reflect malignant disease, including metastatic carcinoma, thorough evaluation to exclude neoplasia is essential. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) serves as a valuable...

item.title: The nanotubular network as a new dimension of intercellular communication in the nervous system
item.description: Communication between cells in the nervous system has long been understood to occur through chemical and electrical synapses, and through the release of signalling molecules and extracellular vesicles across the extracellular space. Intercellular nanotubes (NTs) - thin, membranous tubular bridges that physically connect distant cells - represent a structurally distinct route of communication, enabling the direct, targeted transfer of cellular cargoes between selected cells. Once studied almost...

item.description: Humidity can rapidly alter hybrid-perovskite surfaces, yet the earliest topographic processes linking water adsorption to chemical degradation remain poorly resolved. Here, we tracked the same air-cleaved methylammonium lead bromide (MAPbBr(3)) single-crystal surface using consecutive non-contact atomic force microscopy measurements during a controlled increase in relative humidity (RH). item.title: Associations Between Hospice Care Duties and Compassion Fatigue Among Nurses in Korea: The Roles of End-of-Life Care Stress and Peer Support
item.description: CONCLUSION: Perceived duty difficulty showed a cross-sectional indirect association with compassion fatigue through EOLCS, while its conditional association varied across peer support levels. These findings highlight the relevance of considering perceived duty difficulty together with EOLCS and peer support when examining compassion fatigue among hospice nurses.

item.title: Chronically pressed for time: a grounded theory of time-pressure experiences among perioperative nurses working in operating rooms and post-anesthesia care units in South Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study explains how perioperative nurses continue to fulfill work demands while chronically enduring time pressure, and how their responses and interactions ease or reinforce pressure within this ongoing process. These findings suggest that understanding and addressing time pressure in perioperative nursing requires attention to individual coping alongside the organizational and interpersonal conditions surrounding the work.

item.title: Integrative stratification of response to immunotherapy using host and microbial signatures in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the importance of characterizing dysbiosis using gut microbial signatures, which act along a distinct and complementary axis to explain responses to ICIs.

item.title: The guardians of personhood: a qualitative study of nurses' perspective on person-centred care in the intensive care unit
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Person-centred care in the ICU means caring for the person behind tubes, wires, and machines. It cannot be reduced to checklists or protocols but depends on nurses' ability to pause, notice, and respond, supported by organizational cultures that enable such care. In this way, 'breaking up the frames' is not about dismantling clinical care but expanding it to include the person.

item.title: Health literacy and health outcomes among older adults in Korea: a secondary analysis of 2023 KNHANES data
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The Korean study shows that health literacy is significantly associated with HRQoL and perceived health status. The pronounced gap in the technology and resources domain indicates a key vulnerability in the use of digital health information. Incorporating HL assessment into national health examinations and healthcare settings could help identify individuals with inadequate health literacy who may require prioritized educational support. item.description: Genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) of Campylobacter jejuni (C. jejuni) have been studied mainly for reference strains, and their characteristics at the lineage level remain poorly understood. We reconstructed GSMMs for 86 C. jejuni isolates collected in Korea using gapseq and analyzed them together with in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. item.title: Different osteoarthritis progression rates within early-stage knee osteoarthritis: a retrospective cohort study using machine learning cluster analysis from the osteoarthritis initiative database
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Within baseline KL grade 2 knees, clinically interpretable radiographic phenotypes, including lateral JSN, medial JSN with subchondral sclerosis, osteophyte-dominant changes without JSN, and chondrocalcinosis-dominant patterns, were associated with different 4-year KL grade progression rates. item.description: Mastitis is a major constraint to camel milk productivity, udder health, and milk safety in pastoral and emerging peri-urban dairy systems, yet comparative epidemiological data across these systems remain scarce. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Because the analysis is observational, the estimates are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. The findings highlight the role of implementation depth and organizational fit, and they caution against treating vendor market concentration as inherently efficiency-enhancing.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Mosun-Pola provides profound HRQoL benefits, complementing its superior clinical efficacy and manageable safety profile in patients with ASCT-ineligible R/R LBCL.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The lower rate of extrathoracic progression and prolonged time to progression or death for intrathoracic and extrathoracic (including brain) lesions observed with durvalumab versus placebo further support consolidation durvalumab as the new standard-of-care treatment for patients with LS-SCLC without progression after cCRT.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Psychosocial and structural characteristics contributed to concurrent classification of PHQ-9-defined depression, with exploratory geographic variation in aggregated SHAP contributions. Combining explainable machine learning with spatial statistics may inform further local assessment.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: CLA3+ and CLA4 provide well-calibrated estimates for advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis using controlled attenuation parameter, liver stiffness, and alanine aminotransferase, with small intermediate-risk groups and prognostically informative serial changes. They may serve as second-line tests within Fibrosis-4 index-based two-step pathways.

item.title: Estimating All-cause and Cause-specific Excess Mortality During the COVID-19 Pandemic in South Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The pandemic caused substantial excess mortality in South Korea, concentrated in 2022 and driven mainly by infectious diseases; the peak occurred later than in most high-income countries. The persistence of excess mortality into 2023 and 2024, beyond COVID-19 reclassification, indicates that sustained cause-specific surveillance should remain a public health priority.

item.title: State Capacity and Post-COVID-19 Recovery in Avoidable Mortality and Life Expectancy: A Panel Time-series Analysis Across 38 OECD Countries
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: State capacity was associated with avoidable mortality recovery but not life expectancy recovery. Despite effective early containment, Korea was among the slowest to recover in avoidable mortality, suggesting that outbreak response and essential healthcare continuity may depend on different capacities. Avoidable mortality may warrant monitoring as a health system resilience indicator.

item.description: Population aging affects many aspects of health and social care, particularly the transition of older adults from home-based to facility-based long-term care. item.title: Association Between District-level Aggregate Carcinogen Emissions and Thyroid Cancer Incidence in Korea: An Ecological Study Using Bayesian Spatial Models
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: District-level aggregate carcinogen emissions, predominantly organic solvents by mass, were associated with diagnosed thyroid cancer incidence, most clearly in women. These hypothesis-generating findings may indicate either that as-yet-unidentified chemicals increase thyroid cancer risk or that the models incompletely captured the variables underlying the reported urbanicity-thyroid cancer association.

item.description: Global agriculture faces mounting pressure from climate change, stricter pesticide regulations, and the need to protect crops sustainably. This review examines microbial seed coating and pelleting as strategies for delivering beneficial microbes to suppress soil-borne pathogens and enhance crop vigor. item.description: CONCLUSION: Daily supplementation with L-YLAB improved growth, nutrient digestion, diarrhea status, immune-oxidative balance, gut microbiota, and butyrate production in calves.

item.description: CONCLUSION: IVF accounts for more than half of multiple births in South Korea, with a substantial contribution among women aged ≤35 years. These findings support policies that promote elective single embryo transfer.

The reduced interpretation time in HER2-ultralow BCs further suggests that AI can improve efficiency in diagnostically challenging cases encountered in routine practice.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Despite technical advances, the evidence base remains concentrated at early translational stages. The proposed Translational Readiness Framework provides a structured lens for evaluating progress and guiding research prioritization. Closing the gap between laboratory promise and clinical impact requires a shift from model-centric to patient-centric research and from benchmark performance to real-world validation.

item.title: Associations of factor VIII activity, thrombin generation, and age with joint health in adults with moderate hemophilia A
item.description: CONCLUSION: No clear associations were observed between current FVIII activity or thrombin generation parameters and clinical and radiographic joint outcomes in adults with moderate hemophilia A. The association between age and joint scores may reflect cumulative disease and treatment exposure over time.
